'''Licia Verde''' (born 14 October 1971, Venice, Italy) is an Italian cosmologist and theoretical physicist and currently [[Catalan Institution for Research and Advanced Studies|ICREA]]<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.icrea.cat/|title=ICREA|website=www.icrea.cat}}</ref> Professor of Physics and Astronomy at the [[University of Barcelona]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://icc.ub.edu/|title=ICCUB|website=icc.ub.edu}}</ref> Her research interests include [[Large-scale structure of the Cosmos|large-scale structure]], [[dark matter]], [[dark energy]], [[inflation (cosmology)|inflation]] and the [[cosmic microwave background]].

She received a Laurea degree in 1996 from [[University of Padua]] and a PhD in 2000 from the [[University of Edinburgh]], working with [[Sabino Matarrese]] and [[Alan F. Heavens]]. She did postdoctoral study at [[Princeton University]] and joined the faculty of [[The University of Pennsylvania]] in 2003. From September 2007, Verde is an ICREA Professor at the ICCUB of the [[University of Barcelona]]. She was a Professor II at the [[University of Oslo]] during 2013 to 2016.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.mn.uio.no/astro/english/people/aca/liciav/|title=ITA University of Oslo|access-date=17 December 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160602071805/http://www.mn.uio.no/astro/english/people/aca/liciav/|archive-date=2 June 2016}}</ref> Verde was editor of the Physics of the Dark Universe Journal<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.journals.elsevier.com/physics-of-the-dark-universe/editorial-board/|title=Physics of the Dark Universe Editorial Board|via=www.journals.elsevier.com}}</ref> and is currently scientific director of the [[Journal of Cosmology and Astroparticle Physics]].<ref name="JCAP Editorial Board">{{cite web|url=https://jcap.sissa.it/jcap/help/helpLoader.jsp?pgType=staff|title=JCAP Editorial Board}}</ref> As of 1 January 2019 she is the chair of the science advisory board of the [[arXiv]].

She is known primarily for work on large-scale structure, analysis of the WMAP data and development of rigorous statistical tools to analyse surveys of the universe. She is a highly cited author.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=njSOe-cAAAAJ&hl=en|title=Google Scholar}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/search/q=((%20author%3A%22verde%2C%20l%22)%20AND%20year%3A1997-2020)&sort=citation_count%20desc%2C%20bibcode%20desc&p_=0|title=NASA ADS}}</ref><ref name="hcr.clarivate.com">{{cite web|url=https://hcr.clarivate.com/|title=Highly Cited Researchers - The Most Influential Scientific Minds|website=HCR|access-date=26 May 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190220122703/https://hcr.clarivate.com/|archive-date=20 February 2019}}</ref>

She appeared in the movie ''[[The Laws of Thermodynamics]]'' and is featured in the PBS show [[Closer to Truth]] in its 2020 season.

==Early life and education==
Licia Verde was born in Venice, Italy where she grew up. She attended the [[:it:Liceo classico Marco Polo|Liceo classico Marco Polo]] before she started her undergraduate studies at the [[University of Padua]]. She moved to the [[University of Edinburgh]] in the fall of 1994, first as an Erasmus and later as a PhD student.{{citation needed|date=August 2020}}

==Career==
Verde was a research associate at the Dept. of Astrophysical Sciences, [[Princeton University]] during 2000 to 2003. In 2003, she joined the faculty of the Physics and Astronomy Dept. of the [[University of Pennsylvania]]<ref>{{cite web|url=https://penntoday.upenn.edu/2006-04-13/interviews/where-it-all-began|title=UPENN faculty|date=13 April 2006 }}</ref> and remained there until the end of 2007. Since 2008, she is ICREA Professor of Cosmology at the [[University of Barcelona]]<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.icrea.cat/en/icreas|title=ICREA staff|access-date=7 February 2021|archive-date=23 September 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210923165610/https://www.icrea.cat/en/icreas}}</ref> in Spain. She has also held several faculty visiting positions: Visiting Scholar at the [[Institute for Advanced Study|IAS]] in Princeton, USA (2005);<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ias.edu/scholars/licia-verde|title=IAS Scholars|date=9 December 2019 }}</ref> Visiting Senior Research Fellow at the Dept. of Astrophysical Sciences of [[Princeton University]] (2007-2009); Scientific Associate at [[CERN]] (2012-2013); Professor II of Physics and Astronomy at the [[University of Oslo]] (2013-2016) and Radcliffe Fellow at the [[Radcliffe Institute for Advanced Study]], [[Harvard University]] (2015-2016).<ref name="Licia Verde" /> In 2019 she was appointed chair of the science advisory board of the [[arXiv]] and in 2020 scientific director of the ''[[Journal of Cosmology and Astroparticle Physics]]''.<ref name="JCAP Editorial Board"/>

==Research==
Verde analyzed a powerful but challenging statistical property of galaxy surveys related to higher-order correlations. She showed that the [[2dF Galaxy Redshift Survey|galaxy redshift survey conducted with the Anglo-Australian Telescope]] trace the distribution of [[dark matter]]; this result indicated that the galaxy distribution can be used to study the dark matter one.<ref>{{citation|title=NASA/ADS|bibcode=2002MNRAS.335..432V|last1=Verde |first1=Licia |last2=Heavens |first2=Alan F. |last3=Percival |first3=Will J. |last4=Matarrese |first4=Sabino |last5=Baugh |first5=Carlton M. |last6=Bland-Hawthorn |first6=Joss |last7=Bridges |first7=Terry |last8=Cannon |first8=Russell |last9=Cole |first9=Shaun |last10=Colless |first10=Matthew |last11=Collins |first11=Chris |last12=Couch |first12=Warrick |last13=Dalton |first13=Gavin |last14=De Propris |first14=Roberto |last15=Driver |first15=Simon P. |last16=Efstathiou |first16=George |last17=Ellis |first17=Richard S. |last18=Frenk |first18=Carlos S. |last19=Glazebrook |first19=Karl |last20=Jackson |first20=Carole |last21=Lahav |first21=Ofer |last22=Lewis |first22=Ian |last23=Lumsden |first23=Stuart |last24=Maddox |first24=Steve |last25=Madgwick |first25=Darren |last26=Norberg |first26=Peder |last27=Peacock |first27=John A. |last28=Peterson |first28=Bruce A. |last29=Sutherland |first29=Will |last30=Taylor |first30=Keith |journal=Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society |year=2002 |volume=335 |issue=2 |page=432 |doi=10.1046/j.1365-8711.2002.05620.x |doi-access=free |arxiv=astro-ph/0112161 |s2cid=8140735 }}</ref>

After she joined the science team of the Microwave Anisotropy Probe, a [[NASA]] space mission to map the full sky at radio waves, Verde participated in analysis and interpretation of the Cosmic Microwave Background data from the WMAP satellite.<ref>{{citation|title=NASA/ADS|bibcode=2003ApJS..148..175S|last1=Spergel |first1=D. N. |last2=Verde |first2=L. |last3=Peiris |first3=H. V. |last4=Komatsu |first4=E. |last5=Nolta |first5=M. R. |last6=Bennett |first6=C. L. |last7=Halpern |first7=M. |last8=Hinshaw |first8=G. |last9=Jarosik |first9=N. |last10=Kogut |first10=A. |last11=Limon |first11=M. |last12=Meyer |first12=S. S. |last13=Page |first13=L. |last14=Tucker |first14=G. S. |last15=Weiland |first15=J. L. |last16=Wollack |first16=E. |last17=Wright |first17=E. L. |journal=The Astrophysical Journal Supplement Series |year=2003 |volume=148 |issue=1 |pages=175–194 |doi=10.1086/377226 |arxiv=astro-ph/0302209 |s2cid=10794058 }}</ref>

Verde has been awarded three ERC grants (less than 0.5% of all ERC awardees have achieved three or more ERCs): Cosmological Physics with future large-scale structure surveys (Phys.LSS),<ref name="auto"/>, Beyond Precision Cosmology: dealing with Systematic Errors (BePreSyE)<ref name="auto1"/> and RedTeaming the Hubble Tension (RedH0t)<ref name="auto2"/>. Verde has established a research group in physical cosmology at the University of Barcelona. Under her lead, the group has contributed to results from the Baryon Acoustic Oscillations Survey part of the Sloan Digital Sky Survey: measurements of the expansion history of the universe and the formation of cosmological structures as well as constraint on cosmological parameters describing structure and detailed composition of the cosmos.

The other recent direction of Verde's research is on [[dark energy]]. She has developed a model-independent way to study the Universe's expansion history and infer from there the physical properties of dark energy.<ref>{{citation|title=NASA/ADS|bibcode=2005PhRvD..71l3001S|last1=Simon |first1=Joan |last2=Verde |first2=Licia |last3=Jimenez |first3=Raul |journal=Physical Review D |year=2005 |volume=71 |issue=12 |article-number=123001 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevD.71.123001 |arxiv=astro-ph/0412269 |s2cid=13215290 }}</ref>
